target.title: fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error
target.body:
"## Summary

When a Google generated-video download returns a non-success HTTP response, `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` cancels the unread response body before throwing the error. However, the cancel call was not awaited, meaning the read stream may still be cancelling when the error is thrown. This left the cleanup ordering unproven under asynchronous stream implementations.

This PR adds `await` before the cancel call to ensure the body is fully released before the error propagates.

What changed: Added `await` before `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` at `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts:248`. Also added a regression test (`"cancels unread response body on non-success download response"`) that verifies the cancel is called and the download helper is never invoked.
What NOT changed: No change to success-path behavior, retry logic, timeout handling, or any other part of the provider. No API contract changes.

Fixes #109978

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: On a non-success download response, `response.body?.cancel()` was called without `await`, so the error could be thrown before the stream cleanup completed. Under certain async stream implementations, this could leave the HTTP connection in an indeterminate cleanup state.

**Root Cause**: `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts:248`: `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` — no `await` before the cancel promise.

**Solution**: Add `await` so the cancellation promise settles before the error is thrown. The `.catch(() => undefined)` silently handles rejection cases where the stream was already closed or errored prior to cancellation — this prevents an unhandled promise rejection while preserving the fire-and-forget safety of the original pattern.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic / Node.js v25.9.0 / pnpm vitest 4.1.10

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm vitest run extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts`

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 RUN  v4.1.10 /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
   Start at  06:16:23
   Duration  17.06s (transform 13.85s, setup 529ms, import 16.31s, tests 115ms)
```

The new `"cancels unread response body on non-success download response"` test verifies that:
1. A 403 response triggers `response.body.cancel()`
2. The `bodyCanceled` flag is set to `true` after the `cancel()` completes
3. The download helper is never called (no attempt to download after error)

**Observed result after the fix**: All 17 tests pass including the new regression test. The cancel is now awaited, ensuring proper stream cleanup ordering before the error propagates to the caller.

**What was not tested**: Real Google Veo or Imagen video download endpoint with a genuine non-success HTTP response from the production API. The proof uses a controlled mock response that simulates the cancellation path with a real ReadableStream, which validates the await-ordering correctness but does not exercise the full production fetch/body lifecycle against a live Google endpoint.

## Tests and validation

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

All existing tests continue to pass. The new regression test confirms cancel + throw ordering.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low — one-line `await` addition in a narrow error path, no behavioral change to success path
"
